sources.quote: The federal Multigenerational Home Renovation Tax Credit is a refundable credit worth 15 per cent of up to $50,000 in qualifying costs, to a maximum of $7,500
sources.title: Multigenerational home renovation tax credit (MHRTC) : Personal income tax - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: The Multigenerational home renovation tax credit (MHRTC) is a refundable tax credit that can be claimed for certain renovation expenses to create a self-contained secondary unit. The value of the credit is 15 per cent of eligible expenses or $50,000 (whichever amount is less). If the qualifying expenditures totaled $50,000, it would result in a refundable tax credit of $7,500. The secondary unit must allow a senior or an adult who is eligible for the disability tax credit to live with a qualifying relative.

sources.quote: with financing approved before construction starts and short term rentals excluded
sources.title: CMHC Refinance for Building Secondary Suites |CMHC
sources.evidence: The secondary suite must not be used as a short-term rental (i.e. must not be rented for any period of less than 90 consecutive days). At least one unit must be occupied by the borrower or by a person related to the borrower on a rent-free basis. The maximum number of dwelling units is four units including the existing unit. Insured financing must be approved by CMHC prior to the start of construction or at least at an early stage. Maximum lending value or as-improved property value must be below $2,000,000.

sources.quote: British Columbia's Secondary Suite Incentive Program closed to new applications on 30 March 2025
sources.title: Secondary Suite Incentive Program | BC Housing
sources.evidence: As of March 31, 2025, BC Housing is no longer accepting applications to the program, with the deadline to submit applications being Sunday March 30, 2025. Due to uncertain financial times, and with the federal government committing to implement a similar program, the Province's pilot secondary-suite incentive program will no longer be accepting applications after March 30, 2025. All existing pre-approvals and SSIP mortgages will be honoured.

sources.quote: the Consumer Protection Act, 2023 received royal assent in December 2023 but has not been proclaimed in force
sources.title: Consumer protection laws in Ontario
sources.evidence: In 2023, the Ontario government introduced a new Consumer Protection Act, which when it comes into effect, will renew and update Ontario's consumer protection laws. Until then, the existing Consumer Protection Act, 2002 (CPA), remains in effect. Bill 142, An Act to enact the Consumer Protection Act, 2023, was designated S.O. 2023, Chapter 23 (Ontario Gazette, December 16, 2023).

sources.quote: an estimate forming part of the contract cannot be exceeded by more than 10 per cent without the homeowner's agreement
sources.title: Your rights when starting home renovations or repairs
sources.evidence: Under the Consumer Protection Act (CPA) if an estimate is included as part of a home renovation contract, the final price for all goods and services cannot be more than 10% over the original estimate unless you have agreed to new work or a new price. Any home renovation contract worth more than $50 must be in writing. A customer has the right to a 10 day cooling-off period if they sign a contract at their home.

sources.quote: A contract worth $50 or more signed in the consumer's home carries a 10 calendar day cooling off period
sources.title: Your rights when signing or cancelling a contract
sources.evidence: You always have a cooling-off period when you sign a contract in your home. You can cancel the contract for any reason within 10 days of receiving a written copy of the agreement. For most contracts, the company has 15 days to return your money.

sources.quote: how the 10 per cent construction lien holdback works
sources.title: Construction Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. C.30
sources.evidence: Section 22: Each payer upon a contract or subcontract under which a lien may arise shall retain a holdback equal to 10 per cent of the price of the services or materials as they are actually supplied under the contract or subcontract until all liens that may be claimed against the holdback have expired as provided in Part V, or have been satisfied, discharged or provided for under section 44.

sources.quote: Under BC's Homeowner Protection Act, new homes must be built by a licensed residential builder registered with BC Housing and carry third party warranty insurance, commonly called 2-5-10 coverage
sources.title: Home Warranty Insurance: What Homeowners Need to Know | BC Housing
sources.evidence: All new homes built by a Licensed Residential Builder must have home warranty insurance. All new homes built by licensed residential builders in B.C. must have 2-5-10 home warranty insurance: 2 years on labour and material (some limits apply), 5 years on the building envelope, including water penetration, and 10 years on the structure. BC Housing's Licensing and Consumer Services Branch is responsible for administering the Homeowner Protection Act.

sources.quote: In Alberta, taking a deposit before the work is finished requires a Prepaid Contracting Business Licence
sources.title: Prepaid contracting licence | Alberta.ca
sources.evidence: A prepaid contracting business solicits, negotiates or concludes prepaid contracts in person at any place other than the sellers' place of business and accepts money before all the work is done or the services are provided. Prepaid contractors must be licensed by Service Alberta and post a security.

sources.quote: must show the 10 digit licence number on advertising, vehicles, the website and social profiles
sources.title: Displaying your licence - Régie du bâtiment du Québec - RBQ
sources.evidence: Contractors that hold a licence in good standing must display at all times their licence number on all of their identification and promotion supports. This includes the company's vehicle, in the company's advertisements or in its website or page. Contractors must indicate their licence number on any type of advertising, including business cards.

sources.quote: since June 2025 exterior signage with a non French trademark must show markedly predominant French
sources.title: Modernization of the Charter of the French language | Gouvernement du Québec
sources.evidence: As of June 1, 2025, French must appear in a markedly predominant manner in all signage visible from outside a location that contains a business name in a language other than French or a trademark in a language other than French that is recognized under trademark law and has no French version.

sources.quote: Google retired the Google Guaranteed, Google Screened and License Verified badges on 20 October 2025, replaced them with one Google Verified badge and dropped the money back guarantee
sources.title: About Google Verified badge - Local Services Help
sources.evidence: Effective October 20, 2025, the Google Guarantee green checkmark badge changed to blue and the Local Services Ads references Google Guaranteed, Google Screened, and License Verified by Google changed to Google Verified. As part of this change, Google discontinued the Money Back Guarantee associated with the Google Guarantee badge.

sources.quote: since June 2025 private parties can bring deceptive marketing cases directly
sources.title: Competition Bureau issues a revised bulletin on private access to the Competition Tribunal - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: Starting June 20, 2025, people can directly apply for permission to file an application against businesses under the deceptive marketing practices provisions of the Act. These changes further expand private access to the Tribunal including by allowing applications related to deceptive marketing and by easing the legal test used to determine which applications can proceed.

sources.quote: the profile is a service area business: hide the street address, list your service areas
sources.title: Guidelines for representing your business on Google - Google Business Profile Help
sources.evidence: If you're a service-area business, you should hide your business address from customers. If you don't serve customers at your business address, remove your address and only enter your service area. Service-area businesses can only have one profile for the whole area that they serve.
